local.heading: In Chapel Hill, the university sets the calendar and a big share of the customers.
paragraphs: UNC-Chapel Hill calls itself the town's largest employer, and UNC Hospitals sits on the same campus. The biggest employment sectors in town are educational services, professional and technical services, and health care, which is what you'd expect around a research university founded in 1789. Chapel Hill takes up the southeast corner of Orange County, with a small piece in Durham County. Carrboro borders it on the west and Durham on the northeast, and Raleigh and Durham make up the other corners of the Research Triangle.

That mix changes how people find a business. In a college town, a lot of your customers are new every fall: students, new hires at the hospital, faculty who just moved in. They don't have a neighbor to ask yet, so they search on a phone. A business with a clear site and a complete Google profile is in good position to get that first call, and a customer who starts with you as a freshman can stay for years.

Downtown runs along Franklin Street and the parallel Rosemary Street, where the Downtown Chapel Hill Partnership backs local shops, restaurants and creative spaces. The town and the university have put real money into it. Their 2021 economic development strategy aimed at reviving downtown, UNC leased space from Grubb Properties at 136 Rosemary Street for an innovation hub, and Launch Chapel Hill, one of the university's startup programs, expanded. For a downtown storefront, your website and Google listing are often checked before anyone walks over, so hours and parking details need to be right.

Growth is also moving east. The Town Council created the Ephesus/Fordham District in 2014, now called the Blue Hill District, to bring apartments, shops and offices to the area around Fordham Boulevard and Ephesus Church Road. The Glen Lennox redevelopment sits near where NC 54 meets US 15-501. Meadowmont and Southern Village each have their own village centers. Google treats each of those as its own part of town, and a site that names the ones you serve has a better shot than one that only says Triangle.

industries.heading: Who we build for in Chapel Hill
industries.intro: A university, a big hospital, a busy downtown and newer village neighborhoods add up to a few kinds of businesses that live or die by search in Chapel Hill.

items.name: Medical, dental and therapy practices
items.body: UNC Hospitals and UNC Health offices at Eastowne bring specialists to town, and independent practices compete with that name. Patients want to know if you take their insurance and how soon they can get in. Those answers belong on the page, not in a PDF.

items.name: Restaurants and shops on Franklin and Rosemary
items.body: Business rises and falls with the academic calendar. Menus, hours and event nights have to stay current on the site and the Google profile, especially when students leave in May and come back in August.

items.name: Property managers and real estate agents
items.body: Students, grad students and new UNC staff hunt for housing months ahead, often from another city. Listings, floor plans and a short inquiry form do most of the selling before anyone tours a unit.

items.name: Startups and professional firms
items.body: Consultants, accountants, attorneys and young companies coming out of the university's startup programs. The site has to explain what you do to an investor or a client in one screen.

items.name: Home services
items.body: Contractors, landscapers, cleaners and HVAC companies working the older homes near campus and the newer ones in Meadowmont and Southern Village. Neighborhood pages and tap-to-call bring in the jobs.

includes.title: Edits handled for you
includes.body: Summer hours, a new provider, a new menu. Tell us and we update the site and the Google profile, so what people see matches what they find when they show up.

howWeWork.heading: How we work with Chapel Hill businesses
paragraphs: We're based in Villa Rica, Georgia, west of Atlanta, so Chapel Hill is a long drive for us. Nearly all of the work happens on video calls and in shared drafts. You get a working version of the site to click through on your phone, you send notes, and we make the changes. If a project really needs a day on the ground, we'll talk it through and plan the trip.

You deal with the two people who build your site and run your SEO. No account manager in the middle and no handoff after launch. When something changes at your business, you text or email us, and the same two people handle it.

faqs.q: How much does web design in Chapel Hill, NC cost?
faqs.a: Most Chapel Hill businesses start with our Local Marketing Package: $297 a month, month to month, with no contract. It includes local SEO, paid ads management if you want ads (your ad budget is separate), and a custom website valued at $3,500 at no extra cost.

faqs.q: Can a Chapel Hill business compete with Raleigh and Durham firms in search?
faqs.a: For searches made in and around Chapel Hill, it often can. Google leans on location for local searches. A site that clearly says you serve Chapel Hill and Carrboro, plus a complete Google profile and reviews from local customers, gives you a fair shot against bigger firms that only mention the Triangle.

faqs.q: My business slows down when UNC is out. Can the website help?
faqs.a: It can help you reach the residents who stay year round. We write pages and Google profile posts aimed at families and staff in neighborhoods like Meadowmont and Southern Village, and we can run ads in the slow months if that fits your budget.

faqs.q: Do you work with medical practices near UNC Hospitals?
faqs.a: Yes. Practice sites need provider bios, insurance details, clear service pages and an easy way to request an appointment. We set those up and make sure your Google profile matches, so patients comparing offices on a phone can see what you offer quickly.

faqs.q: Do we ever meet in person?
faqs.a: Usually it isn't needed. We're in Villa Rica, Georgia, and most projects like yours run on video calls and drafts you can review from anywhere. If a project calls for an in-person day, we'll plan one with you.

faqs.q: How long until my new Chapel Hill site is live?
faqs.a: Most sites go live in a few weeks. The pace mostly depends on how fast we get your photos, service details and notes on the draft. If you want to launch before move-in week or a busy season, tell us early and we'll plan around it.
